title: Evalutation of Ocular Symptoms in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis
official: ASSESSMENT OF ISCHEMIC OCULAR CHANGES AND HEMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS IN PATIENTS WITH ASYMPTOMATIC CAROTID ARTERY STENOSIS
summary:
The management of atherosclerotic carotid disease, according to current guidelines, is primarily based on the quantification of the degree of carotid stenosis, together with the assessment of its hemodynamic significance and the presence of neurological symptoms, such as transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke. However, these parameters may not fully reflect the hemodynamic impact of carotid lesions on peripheral vascular territories, particularly the ocular circulation.

The eye represents the only vascular territory that can be directly visualized in vivo, providing a unique "window" into the microcirculation. Retinal and choroidal abnormalities resulting from chronic hypoperfusion may reflect the degree of hemodynamic impairment associated with carotid disease and provide additional information beyond the anatomical characteristics of the stenosis identified by vascular imaging alone.

From a vascular surgery perspective, ophthalmological assessment and fundus examination could allow a more accurate phenotypic characterization of patients with carotid disease, identifying individuals in whom carotid stenosis has already resulted in end-organ microvascular consequences despite the absence of major neurological manifestations. In the era of personalized medicine, such a multidisciplinary approach could move beyond a purely morphological assessment of carotid plaque by incorporating functional and clinical parameters that may potentially contribute to therapeutic decision-making.

The results of the present study may therefore help define the role of fundus examination, combined with a more comprehensive assessment of ocular symptoms, as a complementary tool in the evaluation of patients with carotid stenosis. This approach may facilitate a more accurate identification of patients at higher risk of disease progression and cerebrovascular ischemic events, while potentially improving the selection of candidates for carotid revascularization procedures
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis
* Ocular alterations

Exclusion Criteria:

* Symptomatic carotid artery stenosis
